sentences.text: Hundreds of billions of dollars have been wiped off the value of Nvidia after the US chipmaker announced an independent investigation would be carried out into its chief executive's affair with an alleged Chinese spy.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: The tech firm saw its shares fall by about 4% by close of trade on Monday after Jensen Huang admitted having an extramarital affair.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: Nvidia's probe came after reports that the US believed the Nvidia boss had been targeted in an espionage campaign by China.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: However, China has rejected the claims, with its foreign ministry saying allegations about Chinese spies were "entirely groundless, speculative and intended to smear and malign China".
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the company's secrets or national security were compromised, but a statement by the firm's board of directors said it would begin an investigation in "light of recent reporting that founder and chief executive Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort".
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: US intelligence officials believe Alice Huang, also known as Huang Le, was a spy for Beijing, according to a New York Times report , external .
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: The report said Secretary of State Marco Rubio sent a memo to top officials in Washington last spring warning that the Nvidia boss was in a close relationship with a Chinese spy.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: Alice Huang was managing director of Singaporean company Megaspeed, which has had dealings with Nvidia.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: Jensen Huang admitted he was "unfaithful" to his wife and apologised for hurting her and their children.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: He added he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and would cooperate with the investigation.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: The Nvidia co-founder has also been requested to appear for a joint closed-door briefing for several Congressional committees next week.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: Members of the US House Foreign Affairs Committee last week asked Jensen Huang to appear for a closed-door briefing on his interactions with Alice Huang, as well as Nvidia's security protocols around espionage.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: "Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's [China's] access to sensitive US technology and information," congressmen Brian Mast, John Moolenaar, and Rick Crawford wrote in a letter.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: "It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which US national security has been placed at risk." After Nvidia's investigation was announced, other big tech bosses, including Elon Musk, came out in support of Jensen Huang to continue leading the firm.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: US President Donald Trump said the Nvidia boss was an "honourable guy".
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: However, the news sparked a sell-off in Nvidia's shares, with about $250bn (£190bn) wiped of the company's market value.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: While Nvidia shares fell, the US stock market opened the week on a positive note after last week's turmoil, with Nvidia's rival chipmakers benefiting.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: But analysts suggested the hit to the company would be short-lived.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: Victoria Fernandez, chief market strategist at Crossmark Global Investments said investors would not abandon Nvidia, because the chipmaker was so important to the AI industry.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: "Nvidia is the core of this AI trade, and without them, all these other pieces start to fall apart because the financing's not there," she told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: Jensen Huang co-founded Nvidia, which is central to making the hardware for emerging AI technologies, with two other engineers in 1993.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: Its chips were initially designed for gaming, but he decided to turn its focus on AI development, turning it into the world's second most valuable company.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: A key concern for investors going forward is what would happen to Nvidia if Jensen Huang was removed from the company, as Fernandez said there was "no natural successor" to the chief executive.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: Jensen Huang, unlike other founders in the tech industry, is vulnerable to any move by Nvidia's board of directors to oust him.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: He owns only around 3.5% of the company, and Nvidia operates on a single class voting structure, meaning his stake would not be enough to act as a veto power over any board decision.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: By contrast, many tech founders who lead their companies, including Mark Zuckerberg of Meta and Musk of Tesla and SpaceX, hold significant percentages of multiple types of stock in their companies.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: Even people who do not directly own shares in Nvidia can be affected by rises and falls in its value.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: Pensions or savings invested in pots which have stakes in the company through index tracking funds can be impacted, for example.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: What we know so far about Jensen Huang's affair with suspected Chinese spy Nvidia chips have been a major focus of the AI race between the US and China and the White House has previously imposed controls on where its advanced products can be sold.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: The H200, Nvidia's second most advanced semiconductor, had previously been restricted by Washington over concerns that it would give China's technology industry an edge over the US.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: But Jensen Huang has been against restricting the sale of Nvidia's chips to China, arguing that it would be better for the global rollout of AI to be powered by US technology.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: In January, the Trump administration said it would allow the company to sell its H200 chips to Chinese customers under certain conditions.
sentences.article_title: Nvidia shares tumble over investigation into Huang's affair with alleged Chinese spy

sentences.text: Kashim Chowdhury fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money Aleesha Adams joined a video call with Kashim Chowdhury in May 2023.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: He'd been on sick leave from his job at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) for nearly three months and Adams, his line manager, wanted to put a plan in action to ease him back into work.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: At the start of the call, Chowdhury was coughing and waving tissues up to the camera in an attempt to show how ill he was.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: But what really caught Adams' attention was how pale he looked.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: She noticed white powder had started separating from his forehead.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: "He was sweating, it was like rubbing off, so it was darker underneath and darker on the neck," she told his trial.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: She claimed he was wearing white make-up to look sick.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: Something he denied in court.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: Little did she know UKHSA was not Chowdhury's only employer.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: That month, he was also being paid to work full-time for the Department for the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (Defra), the Department for Business and Trade, the Food Standards Agency and the Home Office.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: He was contracted to work 183 hours a week – more than the number of hours in seven days.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: He fraudulently earned more than £284,000 of taxpayers' money.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: In total, he had eight overlapping full-time public-sector jobs between 2020 and 2023.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: During that time, this relatively junior civil servant was paid £350,000.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: Soon after her call with Chowdhury, Adams discovered that he had logged into the call using a Defra email address.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: When she challenged him about it, he blamed it on a technical error.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: She told the jury at his trial at Southwark Crown Court: "I believed he was lying." She escalated her concerns up the chain.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: But his fraudulent behaviour remained undetected.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: Chowdhury was able to keep working multiple government jobs until September 2023 when he left the Civil Service.
sentences.article_title: How a civil servant got away with juggling five jobs for so long

sentences.text: Michelle Kirsty Reason has been jailed for four years and two months A former police detective who stole more than £85,000 from her own force while working in a team that investigated high-level drugs gangs has been jailed.
sentences.article_title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force

sentences.text: Acting as the exhibits officer and one of only a small number of people with access to a safe that contained hundreds of thousands of pounds, Michelle Kirsty Reason began siphoning off cash in January 2022, Derbyshire Police said.
sentences.article_title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force

sentences.text: According to the force, the 54-year-old spent the money - which had been seized from criminals - on a car, a holiday, and tickets to events.
sentences.article_title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force

sentences.text: On Monday, Reason pleaded guilty to theft and misconduct in public office and was jailed for four years and two months at Mansfield Magistrates' and County Court.
sentences.article_title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force

sentences.text: Detectives said Reason, of Church Lane in Buxton, was a police exhibits officer based in Ripley.
sentences.article_title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force

sentences.text: From about January 2022, the force said Reason began siphoning cash after she dealt with a large cash seizure in the region of £350,000.
sentences.article_title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force

sentences.text: She initially stole £15,000 and told officers that, once she found that nobody had noticed, began taking money on a regular basis until she left the force in December 2025.
sentences.article_title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force

sentences.text: However, officers then began to review the stored exhibits ahead of an upcoming court case, and began to question where the cash had gone.
sentences.article_title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force

sentences.text: Knowing she had been caught out, Reason went to St Mary's Wharf police station to confess to taking the cash.
sentences.article_title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force

sentences.text: She gave a full account of the money that had been taken, even bringing with her the empty evidence bags that cash had been seized in, police said.
sentences.article_title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force

sentences.text: At the crown court hearing in Mansfield, Reason admitted taking £87,174.05, along with €1,620 and £114 worth of Albanian lek.
sentences.article_title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force

sentences.text: Temporary Deputy Chief Constable, Michelle Shooter, said: "Michelle Reason was placed in a position of trust as a detective constable.
sentences.article_title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force

sentences.text: "She broke the trust that we as a force put in her, and broke the trust that the public puts in officers to conduct themselves in a right and proper way.
sentences.article_title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force

sentences.text: "Her actions are a disgrace.
sentences.article_title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force

sentences.text: Individuals who are willing to act in such a way have no place in policing and we will do all we can to root them out and bring them to justice." A further hearing to discuss the case, under the Proceeds of Crime Act, has been listed for 9 April.
sentences.article_title: Detective stole more than £85,000 from police force

sentences.text: The government launched a review into its policy to ban new petrol and diesel car sales by 2035 The UK government's electric vehicle (EV) targets are expected to be reduced this week in a move likely to be welcomed by carmakers but opposed by environmental groups.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Under the current rules, 80% of new cars sold in the UK must be electric by 2030 but industry groups have long called for "urgent relief".
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: New petrol or diesel cars are due to be phased out by 2030 and by 2035 all new cars must be zero emission.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: But the speed of the transition to electric has been hotly debated, including within the cabinet.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: A government source told the BBC it would approach the issue in a "pragmatic and balanced" way.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: If ministers do decide on a steeper watering-down of the rules, it will arguably be interpreted by some - alongside the approval of the Jackdaw gas field in the North Sea - as the government prioritising economic considerations over environmental ones.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Prime Minister Andy Burnham has recused himself from this issue due to his wife's links to an electric vehicle company.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Asked about reports the targets would be reduced, Burnham dismissed this as "speculation", adding: "No decision has been made at this point." Sustainability groups say any weakening of the 2030 target will threaten the UK's long-term electrification and climate goals.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: It could undermine the UK's claim to be providing leadership on climate just as ministers head to Turkey for COP31, the UN's climate summit.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Energy UK, the trade association for the energy industry, has also opposed the move.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: The government's policy to phase out petrol and diesel vehicle sales has undergone multiple changes since it was first introduced by former Prime Minister Boris Johnson in 2020.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: His successor Rishi Sunak pushed back the timeline to 2035, and the Burnham government set up a review of the EV sales targets in August.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: Under the ZEV mandate, the percentage of new car sales that need to be EVs increases each year.
sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.article_title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week

sentences.text: The energy secretary has stressed that affordability is her "overriding objective", as she said reducing bills would be key to maintaining public support for climate action.

sentences.text: Action from "across society" is needed to help improve the educational outcomes of white working-class children, the co-chair of an independent inquiry looking into the issue has said.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: The inquiry's first report, published this summer , concluded that once-in-a-generation reforms were needed to fix a system "not serving the interests of white working-class children".
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: The next phase will focus on early years children and teenagers aged 14 to 19, aiming for a stronger start at primary school and improving older students' routes through education into successful careers.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell said she was "backing" the inquiry to "get to the heart of the barriers holding children back".
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: Inquiry co-chair and former education secretary Baroness Morris said the next phase of the inquiry's work will consider "what needs to be done".
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: "This isn't just the responsibility of schools but calls for action from across society," she said.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: The Independent Inquiry into White Working Class Educational Outcomes , external was commissioned by the multi-academy trust Star Academies, and is supported by the Department for Education.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: It spoke to thousands of young people and their parents, as well as hundreds of teachers.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: Education data about white working class pupils was also analysed as part of the year-long review, looking at the 1.25 million young people in England who are white British and in receipt of free school meals.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: The inquiry found a growing belief among white working-class families that the current education system does not guarantee future success.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: In the summer, the inquiry also acknowledged that the true scale of white working-class disadvantage is "likely to be substantially larger", as the education data they looked at did not include families who were on low incomes but did not receive free school meals.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: Since then, all families receiving Universal Credit have become eligible for free school meals .
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: Under the new phase of the inquiry, practical recommendations for government, schools, colleges and other organisations working with white working-class communities will be developed.
sentences.article_title: Society needs to act to help white working-class pupils, inquiry says

sentences.text: Finnimore believes building the hut was the best option during a cost-of-living and housing crisis An off-grid hut that produces its own heating and electricity can continue to be the home of the man who built it, a council has decided.
sentences.article_title: Hut owner wins battle to keep living in off-grid home he built

sentences.text: Geoffrey Finnimore, a self-employed architectural designer, erected the structure in Glandwr, near Crymych, in 2020, but never told authorities or asked for permission.
sentences.article_title: Hut owner wins battle to keep living in off-grid home he built

sentences.text: Pembrokeshire council told him he must apply for retrospective permission for the home that is self-sufficient, and also collects rain water.
sentences.article_title: Hut owner wins battle to keep living in off-grid home he built

sentences.text: However, the local authority found that because it has now been occupied as a home for more than four years, it is immune from prosecution action.
sentences.article_title: Hut owner wins battle to keep living in off-grid home he built

sentences.text: "Without my home, which I created to solve my own problems and without state assistance, having to pay for other accommodation would be catastrophic for my finances and wellbeing," Finnimore said.
sentences.article_title: Hut owner wins battle to keep living in off-grid home he built

sentences.text: The council asked him to apply for a lawful development certificate , external for the property.
sentences.article_title: Hut owner wins battle to keep living in off-grid home he built

sentences.text: This is a formal legal document confirming the development is lawful.
sentences.article_title: Hut owner wins battle to keep living in off-grid home he built

sentences.text: But as he had lived there for more than four years, it meant he could not be prosecuted, so his application was accepted, the Local Democracy Reporting Service said.
sentences.article_title: Hut owner wins battle to keep living in off-grid home he built

sentences.text: Finnimore has lived in the hut since 2020 but never told authorities or asked for permission Finnimore has been the principal custodian of 4.5 acres of land at Coed Troednoeth, Tir y Gafel since the previous owner left in 2018.
sentences.article_title: Hut owner wins battle to keep living in off-grid home he built

sentences.text: They had lived at the site in a campervan with a lean-to structure, according to the council.
sentences.article_title: Hut owner wins battle to keep living in off-grid home he built

sentences.text: But Finnimore described this as "less than adequate" for his health and wellbeing, so started developing the hut.
sentences.article_title: Hut owner wins battle to keep living in off-grid home he built

sentences.text: This video can not be played Off-grid hut owner wins fight to stay in self-built home In a personal statement to the local authority, he confirmed he had lived at the site for more than 10 years, earns less than £10,000 a year as a self-employed worker, and provided evidence of his long-term residency.
sentences.article_title: Hut owner wins battle to keep living in off-grid home he built

sentences.text: He added: "This application has been sought by the council, and I have had to comply out of a position of vulnerability with respect to the prospect of enforcement against a building and living situation that has been demonstrated to be well-established and that I hold is deemed lawful.
sentences.article_title: Hut owner wins battle to keep living in off-grid home he built

sentences.text: "In the context of a housing and a cost-of-living crisis I have taken care of my own needs.
sentences.article_title: Hut owner wins battle to keep living in off-grid home he built

sentences.text: "So far as the council's responsibilities in that context goes, I see that as one less problem to solve.

sentences.text: Michael Ball attended Dave and Dawn Lloyd's wedding ceremony on Sunday A couple whose surprise radio proposal captured hearts across the country were given an unforgettable wedding gift when singer and broadcaster Michael Ball turned up to perform at their ceremony.
sentences.article_title: Michael Ball's wedding surprise after radio proposal

sentences.text: Dawn Lloyd was shocked when her partner of more than 25 years Dave proposed on BBC Radio 2's Love Songs with Michael Ball programme in the summer and was stunned all over again when the presenter appeared at the couple's wedding at Weston Hall, in Stafford, on Sunday.
sentences.article_title: Michael Ball's wedding surprise after radio proposal

sentences.text: "I had no inkling whatsoever that this was going to happen," she said.
sentences.article_title: Michael Ball's wedding surprise after radio proposal

sentences.text: "I just can't believe Dave has surprised me like this a second time.
sentences.article_title: Michael Ball's wedding surprise after radio proposal

sentences.text: I was fooled the first time and now he has got me again." Ball appeared without warning during the ceremony and performed Love Changes Everything, leaving Dawn and the wedding guests stunned.
sentences.article_title: Michael Ball's wedding surprise after radio proposal

sentences.text: Dawn said the day had been "perfect", with Dave adding he was "grateful for what Michael has done for us as a couple and for all of the family and friends to enjoy it as well".
sentences.article_title: Michael Ball's wedding surprise after radio proposal

sentences.text: This video can not be played Dave said he was "grateful for what Michael has done for us as a couple" Dave and Dawn, from Cannock, won over listeners when Dave secretly teamed up with Ball to stage the proposal.
sentences.article_title: Michael Ball's wedding surprise after radio proposal

sentences.text: Dawn, believing she was taking part in a BBC tour, was welcomed into the studio by Ball, who pretended he was recording voiceovers, before Dave read out a love letter and proposed to the woman he had been with for 31 years.
sentences.article_title: Michael Ball's wedding surprise after radio proposal

sentences.text: During the broadcast, Dave revealed he had already booked the wedding at Weston Hall, choosing a date close to 11 November, the anniversary of the day they first got together.
sentences.article_title: Michael Ball's wedding surprise after radio proposal

sentences.text: Ball later said the proposal was "so moving" that "we thought we have to follow this through".
sentences.article_title: Michael Ball's wedding surprise after radio proposal

sentences.text: Weston Hall holds special significance for the couple and was where Dave first proposed in the late 1990s.
sentences.article_title: Michael Ball's wedding surprise after radio proposal

sentences.text: But Dawn, who was 19 at the time, was so overwhelmed that she laughed, and the engagement ring was later lost, meaning the engagement never officially stuck.
sentences.article_title: Michael Ball's wedding surprise after radio proposal

sentences.text: More than 25 years later, the couple, who now have three children, finally made it down the aisle at the venue where their story began.
sentences.article_title: Michael Ball's wedding surprise after radio proposal

sentences.text: Glenn Gibbins was on trial at South Tyneside Magistrates' Court over a social media post Warning: Some readers may find language in this story offensive A suspended Reform UK councillor has been convicted of a malicious communication over a Facebook post about Nigerian people.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: Sunderland city councillor Glenn Gibbins has been sentenced to a 12-month community order with 150 hours of unpaid work for the "grossly offensive" post made in March 2024.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: It came to light after he was elected to represent the Hylton Castle ward in May 2026.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: Gibbins' post said: "Carnt believe the amount of nigerians in town… should melt them all down and fill in the pot holes!! [sic]" Police were informed about the post after Gibbins was successfully voted in during local elections.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: Prosecutor Emma Dowling said the comment about melting Nigerians down implied they were "somewhat less than human, stripping people in that group of humanity".
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: Godwin Ejeh, a community leader in Sunderland's Nigerian community, gave evidence to say he led a protest outside the City Hall building when Gibbins should have been sworn in, hoping the councillor would apologise.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: However, Gibbins had already been suspended by Reform after the post came to light and he did not attend the ceremony.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: Ejeh, who stood as a Liberal Democrat councillor in the May elections, denied trying to make political capital from the situation.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: He told the court: "We are talking about humanity here, it's way beyond politics." Gibbins, a divorced former salesman who runs a stall in Sunderland city centre which prints novelty gifts, told the court it was a tongue-in-cheek joke.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: "It was an unreal scenario," he said.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: "No-one took it literally." Gibbins recalled on the day he made the post, some Nigerians had approached him about buying some of his printing equipment.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: He said he had "banter" with them at his stall and the conversation had been good fun.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: That night, after "a couple of cans of beer", he said he saw a post on Facebook about Nigerians which he tried to share without success, so he typed it out and posted it to his public Facebook profile.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: He also said he had enjoyed helping residents in the brief period when he was not suspended.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: Summarising the prosecution case, Dowling said the post was grossly offensive and dehumanising.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: She said it was shared "for no reason whatsoever other than to offend and humiliate people from Nigeria who live in Sunderland".
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: Adam King, defending, said the post was "unfunny" and "an unpleasant joke/non-joke".
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: He said professional comedians such as Jo Brand had joked about throwing acid on Nigel Farage and Jimmy Carr about gypsies in the Holocaust and they had not been prosecuted.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: Even if the district judge found the post was grossly offensive, she had to be sure Gibbins intended it to be and could be taken as such, King said.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: Passfield said Gibbins, who has no previous convictions, accepted his post was offensive, but not grossly so, and maintained it was a joke.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: She said it was targeted at a specific ethnic minority and that they could be "eradicated" and turned into inanimate substances and used to fill potholes.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: Passfield said she did not believe the case would have gone to court had he confined his observation to the number of Nigerians living in Sunderland, even if that were a racist-held view.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: But he went on to reduce them to the status of Tarmac, she said.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: His comments were not politically motivated, she added, as there was no wider context about immigration.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: The district judge said she had considered Gibbins' right to free expression as per Article 10 of the European Convention on Human Rights, but decided the post was not a genuine expression of political views.
sentences.article_title: Suspended Reform councillor found guilty over post

sentences.text: Dormice have become much rarer in the UK as woodlands and hedgerows are lost Dormouse numbers may be recovering in England and Wales after years of decline, offering a rare piece of good news for one of our best-loved mammals.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: The animal has disappeared from much of the countryside with conservationists warning of a long-term collapse in its population.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: However, new data suggests dormouse numbers increased between 2020-2025,  a period that coincided with warmer springs and summers.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: Scientists believe these conditions may help dormice survive, by boosting food supplies and reducing the time they spend asleep.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: That gives the animals more opportunity to breed and build up fat reserves ahead of winter.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: Even during spring and summer, when it's cold and wet, dormice can go into short periods of deep sleep But conservationists caution that many questions remain unanswered, and say protecting the woodlands and hedgerows where dormice live remains essential to their long-term survival.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: The only native species of dormice in the UK is the hazel dormouse.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: Once widespread across the country, they are now largely confined to southern England and parts of Wales.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: They have become much rarer as large areas of woodland are lost and so far native populations have disappeared from around 20 English counties.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: The National Dormouse Monitoring Programme, led by the conservation charity People's Trust for Endangered Species (PTES),  has been monitoring sites in England and Wales since 1998.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: It found that since 2000, dormouse numbers have fallen by almost 60%, equivalent to an average annual decline of 3.5%.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: More recently, however, there are signs that trend may be reversing.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: The data suggests the population increased by almost 10% between 2020 and 2025, although researchers stress there is considerable uncertainty around that estimate.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: The apparent improvement coincides with a period of warmer, drier-than-average springs and summers.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: Report co-author Ian White of PTES described the "upturn"  as "welcome good news" which gives grounds for  "cautious optimism".
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: But he added: "We mustn't lose sight of the bigger picture: populations remain almost 60% lower than they were in 2000." The hazel dormouse spends most of its time in trees, coming out at night to eat flowers, insects, berries and nuts The hazel dormouse is famous for spending much of the year asleep.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: It hibernates from around October to May, spending the winter in a nest on the ground.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: Even during spring and summer, dormice can go into short periods of deep sleep, known as torpor, when the weather is cold and wet, or food is scarce.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: This helps the small rodent conserve energy.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: Researchers believe warmer summers may be reducing the need for torpor, leaving dormice with more energy for feeding and breeding.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: They say more research is needed to understand what longer-term impacts climate change could have on the species.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: Dr Charlotte Armitage, an ecologist who worked on the survey, said significant uncertainties remain, including how dormice will respond to warmer, wetter winters.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: However, she said warmer summer conditions are likely to give the animals more energy to reproduce and raise additional litters.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: "This is good news, but we can't be complacent," she told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: "We still need to protect their habitat, do more research into the effects of climate change and carry out effective woodland management for the benefit of dormice."
sentences.article_title: A glimmer of good news for Britain's sleepy dormouse

sentences.text: A passenger on a train where a mass stabbing took place said he initially thought there might have been a suicide bomber, a court has heard.
sentences.article_title: Passenger feared Huntingdon train attacker was suicide bomber, court hears

sentences.text: Milan Campion was travelling on a London-bound LNER service on 1 November last year when it made an unscheduled stop at Huntingdon during an attack by Anthony Williams .
sentences.article_title: Passenger feared Huntingdon train attacker was suicide bomber, court hears

sentences.text: He said Williams was "threatening everyone indiscriminately" so he "came to the conclusion that he wasn't sound of mind".
sentences.article_title: Passenger feared Huntingdon train attacker was suicide bomber, court hears

sentences.article_title: Passenger feared Huntingdon train attacker was suicide bomber, court hears

sentences.article_title: Passenger feared Huntingdon train attacker was suicide bomber, court hears

sentences.text: Kateryna and Mattias have had to postpone their plans to buy a new home A Ukrainian woman who fled to Scotland after Russia invaded her homeland has been told she could face a £9,000 property tax charge because she still owns a flat in Kyiv.

sentences.text: Vinted and eBay could be included in the list of platforms set to be banned for children aged under 16, the culture secretary has said.
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: Lisa Nandy said the government was "looking seriously" at including the retailing websites in the social media ban "to keep children safe".
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: The UK's social media ban for under-16s is set to come into force in March next year, with children barred from accessing platforms such as Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: In response, eBay said it was looking forward to "understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government".
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: Vinted said it welcomed "open dialogue" with ministers and the regulator on the issue.
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: The move was due to fears that messaging functions on the platforms allowed strangers to groom children, according to the newspaper.
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: It suggested similar reselling platforms, Depop and Facebook Marketplace, would also be included in the list of banned sites.
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: Businesses and individuals sell a host of goods on eBay, which has been a major global player in the online reselling market for years.
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: The platform states on its website that it currently requires all of its members to be over 18 years old because listings involve "entering into a contract".
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: Vinted is aimed at over 18s, but its terms and conditions do allow parents or guardians to create accounts for their children, which must be used under parental supervision.
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: The site, on which users mostly buy and sell unwanted clothes and other fashion items, has grown rapidly recently to reach 17 million UK users.
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: A Vinted spokesperson said direct messaging was "part of how the platform works" but that it had a "zero tolerance for harmful or explicit content" and had moderation teams and tools to spot and remove "activity that breaks our rules".
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: "When we identify inappropriate behaviour, we take action, up to a permanent ban or reporting to the relevant authorities," they said.
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: An eBay spokesperson said the company was "focused on providing a trusted and safe marketplace experience for our millions of customers".
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: "While the details of the proposed legislation are not yet clear, we look forward to understanding more and continuing to work constructively with the government," they added.
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: The government announced it would ban under-16s accessing social media in June this year, with children prevented from accessing 10 of the biggest platforms.
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: YouTube will also be banned for under-16s, but YouTube Kids - a version of the video-sharing app designed to be safe for children - will not be included in the measures.
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: A complete list of affected platforms has not yet been released, but the government said it would cover those "whose purpose is to enable social interaction and which allow users to post material".
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: That means platforms that have livestreaming or features that enable the potential for strangers to contact children will also be restricted, which includes gaming sites.
sentences.article_title: Government 'looking seriously' at banning under-16s from Vinted and eBay

sentences.text: It does not mean that Roblox, the biggest gaming site in the UK for those aged eight to 12, for example, will be banned for under-16s.

sentences.text: Is the artificial intelligence (AI) gold rush coming to an end, or is this simply a reality check?
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: That's the question which is hanging over investors, and which has prompted steep falls on the world's stock markets.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: The sell-off in the US on Thursday was most dramatic on the Nasdaq, home to tech industry titans such as Alphabet, Nvidia, Meta and Apple.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: It followed sweeping gains by the Democrats in this week's midterm elections in the US, which have given the party full control of Congress.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: A number of leading Democrats campaigned against the unhindered expansion of data centres, which have underpinned the growth of artificial intelligence.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: Fears this will lead to more regulation of AI appear to have concerned investors.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: But worries about the industry's prospects have been growing for some time.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: The release of Chat GPT by Open AI in late 2022 is widely seen as having generated massive public and corporate interest in the practical uses of AI.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: It also sparked a modern-day gold rush.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: Investors flocked to put their money into companies producing computer chips and  networking infrastructure, building data centres and providing the energy to power them, as well as developing the AI itself.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: The value of tech companies soared.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: The boom continued into this year.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: Investments in AI are expected to reach $1trillion in 2026 alone according to research by Goldman Sachs.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: The sector has scooped up so much available cash that other industries have seen their own borrowing costs increase as a result.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: But investors want returns, and in recent months concerns have been growing about whether the AI boom can produce the expected riches.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: Those worries have emerged at a time when public comments from AI researchers casting doubt over the safety of artificial intelligence - even suggesting it could represent an existential threat to humanity - have been grabbing headlines and fuelling speculation that a clampdown could lie ahead.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: These firms you've never heard of are feeding fears the AI bubble could burst While the Trump administration has been all-in on AI, or "super intelligence" as the president likes to call it, many leading Democrats tapped into grassroots concerns about the expansion of data centres and their impact on local communities.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: These were largely focused on the facilities' high consumption of water and electricity, which many feared would push up their household bills – as well as the noise, use of land, and general disruption associated with them.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: A Gallup poll published in May showed 71% of Americans would oppose the building of a data centre in their community.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: The figure for a nuclear power station was 53%.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: James Talarico, who won the Senate race in once staunchly Republican Texas, was one of those to respond to this scepticism.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: "While we want to protect America's leadership in artificial intelligence, we are still grappling with how it will affect everything from how we work to how our children learn," he said.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: "We must protect Americans and establish clear, consistent laws for businesses." With control of both houses of Congress, Democrats are now expected to challenge the president's technology agenda more vigorously, while introducing legislation which could curb the expansion of the industry.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: Texas' Democratic governor-elect Gina Hinojosa campaigned against data centres, pledging a moratorium on the construction of new facilities.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: Hinojosa's win could present opposition to tech multi-billionaire Elon Musk, who has moved large parts of SpaceX and Tesla's operations to the state, for years a Republican stronghold.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: The Tesla boss had spent nearly $450m to back Republican campaigns in the midterms.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: As the co-founder of the British-based technology firm Arm Holdings, Tudor Brown, points out, "stock values are based on future earnings not present earnings".
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: If the rewards are not likely to be as great as expected, some investors will choose to sell up.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: The falls seen on stock markets over the past 24 hours would appear to have been triggered by the midterm results.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: But concerns that tech firms have become overvalued were being expressed long before the elections.
sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: The question now is whether this is simply the removal of froth from an over-exuberant market, or a sign that the AI rush is a bubble about to burst, with much wider consequences.

sentences.article_title: Why the US midterms sparked an AI stock selloff

sentences.text: The naming of smoky bacon-flavoured crisps has become the latest political headache to emerge from the government's bid for closer ties with the EU.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: The government is negotiating a deal on food standards in a bid to cut costs for British companies trading with Europe.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: Labour ministers have been keen to talk up the potential economic benefits of the agreement, which could be announced at a summit later this month.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: But the deal's requirement for Britain to adopt EU food rules in a wide range of areas has threatened to reignite sovereignty debates from the Brexit era.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: Labour ministers have been keen to sidestep talking about the impact of alignment in particular sectors, instead stressing the overall economic boost it expects the food deal to bring.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: On Thursday, Environment Secretary Angela Eagle told a radio presenter he should "get a life" when he asked about the potential impact of the new rules on snacks, such as smoky bacon crisps.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: But it highlights the political dangers for the government of realigning with regulations that British politicians have not been able to shape, with the Conservatives and Reform UK keen to pounce on cases showing Britain to be a "rule taker" from Brussels.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: It is not the first regulatory skirmish over smoky bacon crisps - following previous headlines over how the well-loved British flavour could be affected by an EU decision in 2024 to phase out a number of artificial smoke flavourings.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: Now, the flavour name itself has been called into question by a separate EU attempt to restrict how descriptions of meat are used to market food.
sentences.article_title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules

sentences.text: This video can not be played Andy Burnham says it isn't fair if an employer 'holds all the cards' Businesses should publish salaries in job adverts now, Prime Minister Andy Burnham is telling firms, rather than wait for a new law to come in that will force them to do so.
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: The government is planning to make pay details compulsory in adverts, with legislation on the issue being brought forward "as soon as possible".
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: It argues the change will help jobseekers, particularly those applying for their first job, and could help prevent pay discrimination.
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: However, one industry group said setting pay was a complex process and regulating adverts was not always suitable.
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: It comes a week after the UK's equality watchdog said employees should legally be able to find out what their colleagues are earning .
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: Burnham said the current system felt "weighted against the applicant" and the changes were aimed at "tilting the scales back".
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: "It can be quite soul destroying for young people these days, applying for jobs when the salary is not listed but sometimes they're not getting a reply," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: The prime minister added that publishing salaries in adverts was also important for closing the gender pay gap.
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: He was also challenged over whether MPs should be disclosing salaries when advertising for staff in their offices.
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: "Whether you're a young person starting out or a parent trying to support your family, you should know what a job pays before spending your time and effort applying for it," Burnham said.
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: The government said the move was part of attempts to reduce the nearly one million young people not in education, employment or training - or "Neet" - ahead of the final report of the Milburn Review into youth inactivity, which is due in the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: Publishing salary details upfront could "expose unjustified differences in pay, give workers greater confidence to challenge discrimination and prevent disagreements over pay escalating into disputes".
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: The proposals are similar to measures being introduced in the European Union. , external Employers in Europe will have to disclose the initial pay or range for new roles, which must either be included in a published job advert or shared before an interview.
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: According to data from UK jobs website Adzuna , external , 51% of the adverts on its site in September had salary information, but the proportion has been falling in recent years.
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: Adzuna co-founder Andrew Hunter said being open about pay "should be the norm, not the exception".
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: He added that employers who put a salary on a job advert "attract more applicants, and better-suited ones".
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: Previous research from the CIPD , external , an industry body for human resources managers, has indicated that the public sector and charities are more likely to reveal pay information that private firms, while pay ranges were more common than specific salaries.
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: But it found not all employers were "fully transparent", with pay ranges sometimes wider than £10,000.
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: CIPD chief executive Neil Carberry said that while, in principle, giving salary details was "a good thing", in practice it was "more complicated".
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: "There isn't always a single fixed figure, and employers will want to set pay based on a candidate's skills, experience and potential." Carberry added the process was complex, saying that drafting job adverts is "best left to good employer practice rather than government regulation".
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: The government has said it will set out further details on what information will be required and how the legislation will be enforced "in due course".
sentences.article_title: PM tells firms to publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law

sentences.text: "It should be up to businesses to decide what information they advertise about job openings, and to decide how to attract the best applicants.

sentences.text: "As long as they are not being dishonest, misleading or discriminatory, it should not be a matter for the government." Last week, the Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC), said publishing salaries in job adverts would be a "positive step".

sentences.text: Tiara Allen arrived on time to interview for a retail job.

sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: Tiara Allen says she took the job despite being made to wait 40 minutes before the interview because she needed work Tiara is far from alone.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: She is one of many people who spoke to the BBC about their worst job interview experiences after we wrote about the one interview question that leaves you feeling uncomfortable .
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: While those situations can be hard to deal with in the moment, they can also teach us a lot about the world of work.

sentences.text: During an interview for an assistant at a book publisher in New York, Chas Edwards was asked a question he wasn't expecting.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: "I was asked for my first job if I was a crier," he recalls.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: Thinking the interviewer was being funny, Chas replied that he didn't cry.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: He was later told that this was why he got the job.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: "Her last assistant had cried – too often, I guess? – and she wanted someone who didn't cry.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: So she was being serious and I thought it was a joke," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: Chas says it was "a terrible, terrible job with a miserable boss" and while he managed to make it through 13 months there without crying he was "crying inside".
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: "I set the world record for working for this person.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: No-one had ever lasted three months with her before," he recalls.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: Despite all this, Chas says he is in some ways grateful the experience was so awful.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: "Because every job since then, even the bad ones, are not that bad," he says, adding that he can "cry anywhere now".
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: Chas Edwards says he thought the interviewer's question for his first job was a joke Corinne Card also found herself floored when the first question she was asked in an interview for an administrative job was if she liked working with people.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: When she replied yes, she was told that the job wouldn't be for her and the interview ended there.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: "I don't know if it was a deliberate trap.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: Because who would answer 'I don't like working with people'?" Corinne Mills, joint managing director of Personal Career Management, says that it can be worth asking an interviewer to clarify any weird questions, perhaps by repeating the question back to them.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: However, if a line of questioning is really off-putting, she says it can also be a sign of what it's like to work there, saying that interviews are also about candidates judging the company.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: Meanwhile, other questions are not just annoying – they are illegal.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: Discrimination against a protected characteristic is against the law , external , meaning an employer cannot treat you less favourably based on your age, disability, gender reassignment, marriage, pregnancy, race, religion, sex, or sexual orientation.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: Employment lawyer Roy Magara says that women being asked if they intend on having children in an interview is a "quite common" kind of bias.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: He says he has also seen a case where an older candidate was told he didn't get the job after an interview because he didn't fit the "vibe" of a younger team.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: If you think these sorts of biases took place in your interview, Roy says you can send the company a subject access request , external to see how they discussed your application internally.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: Worst-case scenarios like these can make interviews feel very difficult, especially considering the control employers have over candidates.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: Euan Cameron, co-founder of hiring software Willo, says that even with this power imbalance it's important not to overthink what an interview is.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: "An interview is just a conversation between two people," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'I was asked if I was a crier': Your worst job interviews revealed

sentences.text: The pigtail is a small spiral at one end of the blade.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Fifoot says that, at the beginning of the cooling process, this spiral "chokes" the flow of solidifying crystals so that just one takes over.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A bit like a hairpin corner in an F1 race right before the finish line – one driver can take the lead here and go on to win.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "Sometimes we need to play around with the number of turns or the angles on [the pigtail] to try and get more favourable grain," adds Fifoot.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Once the blade is formed, this crucial but sacrificial spiral is cut off.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: France's Safran is among the few companies that can make single crystal blades Blades made by Rolls-Royce are used in aircraft engines including the Trent XWB-84, which powers the Airbus A350-900, and the Trent 1000 XE, for the Boeing 787.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The single crystal is essential to ensure each blade's performance.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Sometimes a blade doesn't cool quite as planned, for example two crystals form within it instead of just one, and the metal alloy must be reprocessed so that the manufacturer may re-use the material.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Special ceramic coatings also protect blades from extreme temperatures inside engines.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And another important feature is that blades are cast with tiny channels that allow a flow of cooler air to coat them in a kind of film while the aircraft engine is working.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "The drive at the moment [across the industry] is currently to make those cooling passages really intricate," says Paul Withey, at the University of Birmingham, who formerly worked for Rolls-Royce.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The more turbulent those little flows of cool air are, he explains, the more they will knock heat out of the surrounding, much hotter air.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: And blade-makers also seek to reduce the mass of these components as much as possible.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: "If we can take any weight out of it, you can run that engine more efficiently using less fuel – you can spin it faster and hotter," says Fifoot.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: The turbine blades are used in the Trent 1000 engine among others Meanwhile, China hopes to become only the sixth country to master the whole technology chain for single crystal blade casting.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: A report in May , external quoted one engineer at the AECC Beijing Institute of Aeronautical Materials claiming that China now had a single crystal alloy "superior to or equivalent to the second-generation single-crystal superalloys widely used in Europe and the US".
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: It costs less to make, too, apparently.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: But the West has a "huge advantage" over China given that the majority of commercial airliner production happens there, says Sweetman.

sentences.text: Supply chains and the latest innovations are generally clustered in the West.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Plus, Western manufacturers also have lengthy safety records under their belts.
sentences.article_title: The engine parts that 'fight the laws of the universe'

sentences.text: Then, the other would have to follow suit in order to remain competitive.
