sentences.text: Managing AI agents is a big part of Lotte Underwood's job Recent university graduate Lotte Underwood is a public relations executive with a twist - she spends more time using AI than actually doing PR.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Underwood, 25, joined London-based PR agency Fight or Flight in November last year, in the new role of "AI associate" after completing a degree and then a masters in marketing.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: She's part of a recently established, dedicated AI team that has built around 30 AI agents.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Specific tasks include industry research, client reporting, media interview preparation, helping clients create clearer briefs, and image generation.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: A big part of Underwood's job is to manage those agents, check their outputs and feed those to the team members who are dealing directly with clients and the media.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Another key responsibility of hers is to monitor how clients appear in the responses from AI tools like ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and others.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "A huge part is being in client meetings and calls to work out what is actually going to be most helpful from these agents," says Underwood.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: AI is seen as one of the main factors behind graduate job cuts , but companies are also creating dedicated AI-specific graduate roles like Underwood's.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Dillan Patel, for example, joined engineering software company Stride 18 months ago as an intern.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: A business management graduate, he was put to work developing an internal chatbot designed to capture the knowledge of a senior staff member transitioning into retirement.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Patel, 24, is now an AI automation analyst, tasked with developing further internal agents to provide specific information to individual teams, while also identifying which manual or repetitive tasks across the company could be done by AI.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "My role focuses on finding practical ways to use technology, automation, data and AI to improve how we operate," says Coventry-based Patel.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Debra Maxwell is looking for "AI disruptors" Such AI savvy graduates are also in demand from companies like ArvatoConnect, an outsourced contact centre company.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: CEO Debra Maxwell says the company's usual graduate intake is on hold this year, but she plans to resume it next year with a bigger focus on AI.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "We would be looking for more AI-disruptor type roles, where you can challenge us as an organisation to think more holistically about where AI can be applied and where we could grow our business from," says London-based Maxwell.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "We see our graduates as not filling administrative roles, but actually adding value to the organisation in a different way." Maxwell adds: "For example, one of our recent graduates is using AI to do deep dives on specific markets, and provide more information for when we're bidding [for new contracts].
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: It's basically giving him a more rounded role." If AI can make a graduate job bigger and more integral to the organisation, Maxwell argues that companies can create a more loyal, engaged workforce that is able to contribute more meaningfully, much earlier.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Research from consultancy PwC found that some graduate roles are assuming more responsibilities because of AI, as it allows companies to demand more senior abilities from junior hires.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: For the consultancy's 2026 AI Jobs Barometer , external , it analysed 2.4 million entry-level jobs in the US.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: It found that the entry-level roles most influenced by AI are now seven times more likely to require traditionally senior-level skills.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: These include motivational leadership, strategic decision making and team building.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Those entry-level roles with higher expectations have in fact grown 35% since 2019, PwC found, while other entry-level roles actually shrank by 10%.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Cian Clinton uses around ten AI agents for work tasks Cian Clinton, who joined consultancy Valliance last September after graduating from a Bachelor of Science in 2024, says the incorporation of AI into his role makes him feel less like a graduate, and more like an equal team member.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: He uses around 10 AI agents daily for different tasks.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "Your ideas and your creativity are a lot more valued because you actually get to implement those firsthand, and the responsibility you take on is a lot greater because of that," says London-based Clinton, 23.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "I am now taking on responsibilities which would usually take me four or five years to get to." His career progression, he believes, will now be faster as a result.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "AI is killing the 'pyramid' approach…progression is no longer based on your knowledge bank.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Now it's more based on your critical thinking and understanding of the processes," says Clinton.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: There's no doubt Underwood, Patel and Clinton are developing valuable AI knowledge which can help them across their careers.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: But with their time at work so focused on AI, does it matter how much - or how little - time they're spending learning about the professional field they're supposed to be operating in?
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Underwood says she'd like to still pick up the traditional PR skills her role isn't currently focused on, but is confident of her future in the agency's growing AI team.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "There's certain things that I haven't had the chance to do yet, like directly pitching to the media.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: I absolutely plan to do this," she says.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Graduates becoming too AI-centric is an issue for Simon Pratt, chief operating officer at Portman Finance Group.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: He says being able to use AI effectively is important, but the company's two-year graduate programme is fully centred on "learning the trade".
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "Our graduates rotate across four areas at six-month intervals, working directly alongside senior relationship managers to learn their trade," Northampton-based Pratt explains.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "They'll learn all of our financial products, how to draft credit papers for submission to lenders, and how to build meaningful relationships with our customers.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: They'll progress to running transactions from start to finish." Claire Reid, PwC UK's chief technology and innovation officer, believes graduate roles that are too AI heavy won't necessarily provide graduates long-term career progression.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "There will be no graduate job now that doesn't require a baseline of AI literacy," says Glasgow-based Reid.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "But AI skills on their own are not going to help you in your career.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: You've got to couple that with that sector knowledge of what that client actually wants." Back in Coventry, Dillan Patel is confident his AI work will continue to be valuable, and he wants to keep building on it.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: "I don't think I'd want to explore different positions within the business.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Through my involvement in AI-related projects, I already work closely with different areas of the business and I'm gaining valuable knowledge and experience along the way," he says.
sentences.article_title: Graduates are managing AI - but are they learning much else?

sentences.text: Amazon Prime Air is expanding to 500 US towns and cities Nature lover Ashley Schmidt no longer spends much time in her garden, in the Dallas suburb of North Garland.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: She's also given up on cycling to the local parks where she previously enjoyed taking close-up photos of the bugs, lizards and toads.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It's all because she can't stand the sound of the delivery drones that fly overhead, depositing her neighbours' online orders.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "They emit this very annoying buzz.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It triggers my fight or flight response," says the 44-year-old administrative assistant.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "You can hear the drones on approach and you can hear them inside your home when they pass directly overhead and then you hear them as they leave," she says.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Amazon says it is working to reduce the noise of its drone fleet Schmidt is one of a growing number of people living with the noise of drones dispatched by companies including Amazon and Walmart as they seek to speed up home deliveries.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Delivery drone services, not long ago a novelty, are becoming part of everyday life for many people in the US.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Among them, Amazon Prime Air is in the process of expanding deliveries to nearly 500 cities and towns, delivering items that fit into a space the size of a shoe box.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It has also launched to customers in and around Darlington in the north of England.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Smaller drone delivery services are popping up too: in some US cities, customers can order flying treats from their local pizza joint or ice cream parlour.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Even in cities where noise is already a steady part of life, the sound of drones seems to irk in a particular way.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: While the steady passing of traffic might blend into the background, the sudden whine of a drone's rotors can pierce the everyday hum.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The sound tends to be "particularly noticeable, even when overall sound levels are relatively low," says Antonio Torija Martinez, professor in acoustic engineering and psychoacoustics at the University of Salford.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Unlike planes, drones operate at low altitudes and may fly directly over residential areas.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "They can expose communities that have not previously experienced significant aircraft noise, and who may therefore be more sensitive to changes in their local soundscape," says Torija Martinez.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: He points to research showing that people respond strongly to a noise when they consider the source to be "novel, intrusive or frequent".
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: People who benefit from a drone delivery service, for example, may be less bothered by the noise.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The FAA says operators and local community leaders have primary responsibility for addressing any community concerns.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Greenjets encloses some of the blades on its drone inside a pod Might better technology muffle the irritating buzz?
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: One startup, Greenjets, set out to tackle both "noise level and the frequency of that noise," as Darren James, future technologies lead at the company, puts it.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The London-based business has designed a propulsion system it claims can reduce drone noise by at least two thirds.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: While standard drones use spinning propellers that slice through open air, creating that high-pitched buzz, Greenjets encloses spinning blades inside a pod, to muffle the sound and direct the noise away from the ground.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Its system also quietens things down through slower rotor speed and by using materials that reduce vibration noise.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Making quieter drones isn't just about keeping the noise down for neighbours who are already sick of airborne deliveries.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Greenjets' low-noise tech has been used by police and harbour security teams in Germany.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It has also helped conservationists in Africa, who are seeking to track poachers from above without being detected.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Battlefield drone operators also have good reason to keep the noise down, to avoid alerting the enemy of the approach of their unmanned vehicles.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "There are some efforts to reduce the sound of drones.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: The US Special Forces are interested, at an experimental stage," says Robert Tollast, a research fellow at Whitehall think tank The Royal United Services Institute (RUSI).
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: But he stresses that drone speed, rather than stealthiness, tends to come first for larger drones used in the war between Russia and Ukraine.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "Make it faster, not less quiet, seems to be the approach," says Tollast.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Sharrow Engineering developed twisted propellers that reduce noise For Detroit-based entrepreneur, Greg Sharrow, it was the challenge of broadcasting a classical music performance back in 2012 that set him on the path to quieter drone design.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: He needed to film a violinist from a tricky angle and a drone seemed the only solution – except that it would be far too noisy.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: As a starting point, "I knew that most of the noise from the drone was coming from the propeller, not the motor," he says.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Specifically, it was the tips of the blades that he realised were creating the noise as they swiped through the air.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "I asked myself a very simple question, what would a tipless propeller look like and how would it function?" The result was to create a propeller with twisted loop-shaped blades with no points.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It turned out it was easier to test his propeller in water than it was to repeatedly fly a drone, which led Sharrow to initially develop a less noisy boat propeller.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Now, however, his company, Sharrow Engineering, is focusing on developing "ultra-quiet" drone rotors.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "We have validated that the technology works in drone applications and that it is dramatically quieter," says Sharrow.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Companies at the forefront of drone deliveries say they are also working to reduce the noise of their fleets.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: A spokesperson for Amazon says it has made "measurable sound improvements" to its drones and its latest designs use custom-designed propellers "that produce almost half the perceived sound of the prior generation, with a milder tone".
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: Drone maker Wing, which provides its vehicles for Walmart deliveries, says its propellers are designed to minimise noise.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: It also varies its flight paths to prevent repeated overflights over any single home or neighbourhood.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: For Schmidt, fed up with the noise of drones, the only truly satisfactory solution would be to halt drone deliveries in her area.
sentences.article_title: 'An annoying buzz': The search for stealthier drones

sentences.text: "I would like them to completely stop until they figure out how their services stop being a nuisance," she says.

sentences.text: Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood set out the plans in the House of Commons Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has set out plans to overhaul immigration rules.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Proposals for stricter requirements to qualify for permanent settlement in the UK were first outlined in detail in November 2025, when Mahmood was home secretary in Sir Keir Starmer's government.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: She has argued that settlement should be "earned", rather than being granted automatically, with those who contribute more to the country able to settle fastest.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Following a consultation , external , Mahmood has now announced her final decision on what changes should be taken forward.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Elements of her original proposals have been revised following a backlash from some Labour MPs, with plans to make foreign care workers already in the UK wait 15 years to qualify for settlement scrapped.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Mahmood scraps settlement plans for migrant care workers Labour MPs pull their punches on immigration changes Indefinite leave to remain (ILR) – also known as settlement – gives someone the right to live, work and study in the UK for as long as they like.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Under the current system, people with ILR can also apply for benefits if they are eligible.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: People who have lived in the UK for 12 months after being given ILR can apply for British citizenship, if they also meet other requirements , external .
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Under the government's plans, the standard length of time migrants will have to live in the UK to qualify for permanent settlement will double from five to 10 years.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Under this 10-year pathway, applicants must have earned at least £12,571 for five of the seven years immediately before being granted settlement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Migrants who have claimed certain benefits or breached immigration rules will only be able to settle after at least 20 years.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Adults with a criminal record will be refused settlement, with discretion to refuse cases where the offence was committed when the applicant was under 18.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Refugees who arrived in the UK through an official government scheme will qualify for settlement after five years.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: However, other refugees will need to wait 10 years and either work or study.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Those who do not work or study will need to wait 20 years.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Refugees who arrived in the UK by small boat or another illegal route will have to wait 20 years if they work or study, and 30 years if they don't.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: The changes will apply to migrants who are already in the UK but not those who have already been granted settlement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: A partner who arrives with someone who then applies for ILR will be able to settle at the same time, as long as they meet the relevant requirements.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: However, a partner who joins later will need to complete the same qualifying residence period before they are eligible for settlement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Eligible couples will be able to combine their earnings to meet the minimum income  requirement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: The household income threshold will be £25,142 – twice the individual minimum income requirement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Children under 18 will continue to be able to settle with their parents.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: They will be exempt from the income, government debt, English language and Life in the UK test requirements, but will remain subject to the relevant suitability and criminality requirements.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Young adults aged 18 to 24, who remain dependant on their family, will also continue to be able to settle alongside them.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: They will be expected to meet all the adult mandatory requirements but not the individual income requirement.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Someone who is aged 25 or over when their family becomes eligible for settlement will be expected to qualify independently.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Eligible partners, parents and children of British citizens will continue to qualify for settlement after five years.
sentences.article_title: What are the planned changes to immigration rules?

sentences.text: Concerns have been raised with the government about the amount of time primary school children are spending on a game designed to make learning times tables fun.

sentences.text: TT Rockstars, which allows children to compete with their classmates for virtual coins and rock-star themed characters and outfits, is widely used by schools for maths homework.
sentences.article_title: Children spending too long on maths app TT Rockstars, MP warns

sentences.text: Labour MP Emily Darlington said the app and others like it could be harming children's development because it rewards them for "length of time rather than quality of time spent online".
sentences.article_title: Children spending too long on maths app TT Rockstars, MP warns

sentences.text: Bruno Reddy, founder of the firm behind TT Rockstars, said he shared concerns about screen time and was working with schools to bring in curfews and time limits.
sentences.article_title: Children spending too long on maths app TT Rockstars, MP warns

sentences.text: He said the company discourages long sessions, adding: "Every game in TTRS is deliberately short, and our characters remind children to take regular breaks.
sentences.article_title: Children spending too long on maths app TT Rockstars, MP warns

sentences.text: "The rule of thumb we give schools is: three minutes, four or five times a week.
sentences.article_title: Children spending too long on maths app TT Rockstars, MP warns

sentences.text: In September, a typical child played on three days, for about six minutes each time." He said that from 24 November "every school will have a curfew and a daily time limit switched on, and leaderboards switched off as default".
sentences.article_title: Children spending too long on maths app TT Rockstars, MP warns

sentences.text: "Parents are concerned that this causes conflict on time spent on devices and the pressure to perform against classmates," she added, and this could deter them from taking part in real life, rather than screen-based, activities.

sentences.text: The Milton Keynes Central MP raised concerns about TT Rockstars on Tuesday at the Commons Science Committee, which is investigating the impact of screen time and digital devices on children's brain development.

sentences.text: The company behind TT Rockstars, Maths Circle, says that the app and a similar programme for addition and subtraction, Numbots, is used in 17,000 schools and over 100,000 households.
sentences.article_title: Children spending too long on maths app TT Rockstars, MP warns

The government is in the process of drawing up guidelines for schools and parents on the amount of time five to 16-year-olds should spend on screens.

sentences.text: So it's profit driven." He said there were "ways of making learning fun" that did not involve "competition with yourself or with someone else" and EdTech should be about supporting teachers and not replacing them.

sentences.text: New blood tests designed to check for multiple cancers in one go will be offered to NHS patients in some 200 GP surgeries in England as part of a trial.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The aim is to detect hard-to-diagnose abdominal cancers, including liver, ovarian and pancreatic cancer, much sooner.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: These cancers are often found only after they have spread.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The tests look for proteins or fragments of DNA in the blood that may signal cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Results could help doctors decide which patients with vague symptoms need further investigations.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: More than 20,000 patients aged 45 and over with symptoms such as pain or persistent bloating will be eligible to take part.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The government-funded trial, led by the University of Birmingham, will assess whether the tests are accurate enough for wider NHS use.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The idea of a blood test that can identify multiple cancers is not new.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: A separate NHS trial of a test called Galleri recently failed to meet its main goal of reducing diagnoses of late-stage cancers, although researchers are still assessing its potential benefits.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Prof Peter Johnson, NHS England's national clinical director for cancer, said detecting abdomen cancer early was "notoriously difficult" because symptoms can easily be mistaken for other less serious conditions.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Earlier diagnosis gives patients a much better chance of successful treatment and survival.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Around 71,000 people in England are diagnosed each year with pancreatic, stomach, liver, ovarian or bowel cancer, and nearly 35,000 die from these diseases.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: The new STRIDE-RCT trial , external is about detecting bowel, small bowel, stomach, oesophageal, pancreatic, liver, bile duct and gallbladder, ovarian, endometrial, kidney, bladder and prostate cancer.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Patients will provide one or two tubes of blood, taken at their GP practice, alongside routine tests.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Scientists will then analyse the samples for signs of cancer and, if present, may be able to pinpoint where in the body the tumour is located.
sentences.article_title: 'Multi-cancer' blood tests coming to some GP surgeries soon

sentences.text: Eating fruit and vegetable scraps such as peels and stalks could provide a health boost that most of us are missing, say UK researchers , external .
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: They say scraps are an overlooked source of dietary fibre and are encouraging people to try "root-to-tip" eating, including watermelon rind, pineapple core and butternut squash seeds.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Most adults do not get enough fibre.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Official figures , external show only 4% meet the recommended 30g a day, despite its well-known benefits for gut health.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Fibre aids digestion, helps you feel fuller for longer and is linked to a lower risk of heart disease and bowel cancer. , external Skin and pips can be beneficial, the fibre researchers say As a rule of thumb, the skins of fruit and veg pack more fibre than the insides.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Eating a kiwi with the skin on , external provides 50% more fibre than having a peeled one, for example.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: For their study, the scientists at King's College London analysed 12 raw or uncooked fresh foods - beetroot, bell pepper, broccoli, butternut squash, cauliflower, celeriac, curly kale, fennel, kiwi fruit, leek, pineapple and watermelon.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Project lead Dr Rachel Gibson said the findings suggested people are throwing away a significant amount of fibre.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: "This isn't just a nutritional loss, it's also a financial one - you're effectively throwing away a substantial portion of what you've paid for." King's College London has been experimenting in its canteen , external , offering staff and students root-to-tip meals, such as banana skin curry.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: At home, people might want to try leaving skins on kiwi fruit, using broccoli stalks in stir-fries or adding bell pepper seeds to dishes, the researchers suggest.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: While cooking can change the fibre content, it doesn't usually destroy it all.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Steaming, microwaving or quick sautéing tends to preserve nutrients best .
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Gibson said: "This isn't about perfection and this isn't about forcing people to eat unpalatable food – it's about recognising the nutritional value in components we've been conditioned to discard." She acknowledges some may be hesitant to try it.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Some diners raised concerns during the canteen trial.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Kirsten Jackson, a dietitian with the British Dietetic Association who specialises in irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), says the food hacks are useful as long as produce is washed thoroughly.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: She suggests blending pineapple cores into smoothies, but says the tough skins are not something she would recommend.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Some stalks may need to be cooked or finely chopped to make them more palatable, she adds.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: "Just because a broccoli stalk doesn't fit into tonight's meal doesn't mean it needs to go in the bin.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Chop it up, freeze it and add it to a soup or stir-fry another day," she said.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: She advises increasing fibre intake gradually to avoid bloating, noting that people who have IBS may find it harder to tolerate.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: And there are some things to avoid entirely, said the British Nutrition Foundation.
sentences.article_title: Biggest fibre boost could be scraps in your bin, experts say

sentences.text: Consultant doctors in England are to stage a two-day strike next month in a dispute over pay and working conditions.

sentences.text: The walkout will begin on 25 November at 06:59 GMT, with consultants staffing emergency care only.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: This is known as Christmas Day cover and is likely to have a major impact on most routine and elective or planned services.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The announcement comes after talks had been taking place with the government over the past month, following the vote in favour of strike action by British Medical Association members in July.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Consultants – the most senior doctors in hospitals – were given a 3.5% pay increase this year.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: But the BMA argues pay has fallen by a quarter over the past 17 years, once inflation is taken into account.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: The union also wants a reduction in the standard working week, from 40 to 35 hours, and higher pay for out-of-hours work, alongside changes to pensions, including greater flexibility over when they can be taken.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: In a joint statement, BMA consultants committee co-chairs Dr Helen Neary and Dr Shanu Datta, said they had tried to negotiate with the government in "good faith", but "time-and-time again ministers have kicked the can down the road".
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: "Unfortunately, that road has now run out, and we have been forced to announce strikes.
sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: "Consultants take their responsibilities incredibly seriously, and striking does not come naturally, but we are hearing loud and clear from the profession that they have had enough." Average earnings for consultants top £150,000 a year.

sentences.text: Basic pay starts at £113,500, with the most experienced getting £150,500.

sentences.article_title: Consultant doctors in England to strike next month

sentences.text: Irene Breen told the BBC her business suffered a significant financial hit from the restrictions When Irene Breen got a notification in January 2025 that Instagram was removing adverts for her company's pregnancy pillows, she was confused.

sentences.text: What was so offensive about a pillow?
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: She was later told on a call with Meta that the problem was the word "pregnancy".
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: "We had to scrub the word from our entire website… from the product name," Breen said.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: "We had to remove all our URLs which had pregnancy in them and rename them all." The restrictions were eventually lifted but, she said, it took 10 months of conversations with Instagram's parent company Meta - by which time her business had suffered a significant financial hit.

sentences.text: Meta, which also owns Facebook, told the BBC that while businesses can run adverts that promote wellness, sexual health and reproductive products and services, there are restrictions to avoid users across countries and cultures having a negative experience.

sentences.text: The company initially declined to comment on individual cases.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: After the BBC’s story was published, a spokesperson added: “The suggestion that the word 'pregnancy' cannot be used on our platforms is incorrect.
sentences.article_title: Our business ads were taken down for saying 'pregnancy' on Instagram

sentences.text: To be clear, people can freely use the word 'pregnancy' in posts, and share and discuss pregnancy-related content.” It's not just businesses taking out paid adverts who claim their content has been unfairly restricted.

sentences.text: An emergency vaccination programme followed an outbreak in Kent A vaccination programme targeting one million teenagers and young adults is being launched, after concerns about the number of meningitis B infections.

sentences.text: Teenager's family 'heartbroken' by meningitis death Meningitis B vaccine to be offered to a million young people Meningitis is an infection of the protective membranes that surround the brain and spinal cord.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It can affect anyone but is most common in babies, young children, teenagers and young adults.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It can be very serious if not treated quickly.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The cause of the infection - either certain bacteria or viruses - can be determined by tests.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Bacterial meningitis is rarer but more serious than viral meningitis.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It can lead to blood poisoning or sepsis, and can affect the brain.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: This acute, severe infection is known as invasive meningitis.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It means the infection has invaded the blood stream or brain linings.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Meningitis B, or MenB, is behind most cases of more severe meningococcal disease in the UK.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Cases happen every year - in 2024-2025, there were 378 cases of invasive meningococcal disease, according to official data.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Symptoms can develop suddenly and can include: a rash that doesn't fade when pressed with a glass sudden onset of high fever severe and worsening headache extreme sleepiness/difficulty waking Two vaccines protect against the main causes of meningitis and septicaemia.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The MenACWY vaccine offers protection against four types of bacteria that can cause meningitis - meningococcal groups A, C, W and Y - and is offered to teenagers aged 14 years old.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Anyone who missed out can get it for free until their 25th birthday.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine helps protect against meningococcal group B bacteria and is recommended for babies aged eight weeks, followed by a second dose at 12 weeks and a booster at one year.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The vaccines do not contain any live bacteria and cannot cause meningitis.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Meningitis can sometimes occur as a complication of some other infections, meaning several other vaccinations can also help protect people.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: A six-in-one vaccine given to young children - also known as the DTaP/IPV/Hib/Hep B vaccine - offers protection against diphtheria, tetanus, whooping cough, hepatitis B, polio and Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib).
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: A pneumococcal vaccine offers babies protection against serious infections caused by pneumococcal bacteria, including meningitis.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The MMRV vaccine - which replaced the MMR vaccine in January 2026 - offers infants protection against measles, mumps, rubella and chickenpox.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The MMR vaccine is free for anyone who missed getting it when they were younger, regardless of their age.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Generally, it takes a couple of weeks to get full protection from a vaccine and some require booster doses.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The MenB vaccine was added to the UK NHS childhood immunisation programme for babies born on or after 1 July 2015.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: That means teenagers and young adults over the age of 11 have not received this jab.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Young babies are vaccinated because they are more likely to get invasive infections more often than other age groups, and their bodies are less likely to be able to fight them off.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: However, research suggests the MenB vaccine doesn't necessarily prevent transmission of the infection from person to person, doesn't target all the different B bacteria strains and doesn't provide very long-term protection.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: But UK vaccine experts now say government should consider routinely offering the vaccine to all teenagers at around age 15 .
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It will be up to ministers in each nation to decide whether to do this.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Additionally, one million young people are now being offered the MenB vaccine in a one-off, targeted programme this summer to help protect them.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: All Year 13 pupils - meaning those who could soon leave for university - and anyone under 25 who is starting university or residential further education for the first time this autumn, will be able to get two doses of the vaccine for free on the NHS.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Experts say this population is at higher risk of potentially catching meningitis B which can spread when people live together in shared accommodation.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Invasive meningococcal disease tend to peak in October to November each year, which further heightens the risk.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Some people carry the bacteria in their nose or throat without getting sick, but can spread it to others through the exchange of spit or saliva in coughs, sneezes and kissing, or by sharing vapes and drinks.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Close personal contact is necessary for spread to happen.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The infection can also be spread by someone with meningitis, although this is less common.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: It's possible to get meningitis more than once.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: The best way to stop the disease spreading is to give antibiotics to people who may have come into contact with it.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Vaccination can also provide some protection from future infection.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Anyone becoming unwell with symptoms of meningitis or sepsis should seek medical help urgently at the closest Accident and Emergency Department or by dialling 999.
sentences.article_title: What are the symptoms of meningitis and how is it spread?

sentences.text: Early treatment can be lifesaving.

sentences.text: Dr Afifa Qazi from Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust said the opening was an important step forward The first NHS intensive care unit for women with serious mental health needs in Kent and Medway is due to open.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: Women in the region will have access to a dedicated NHS psychiatric intensive care unit for the first time, following a £4.63m investment by Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: The 10-bed facility at Littlestone Lodge in Dartford will provide short-term, intensive care for women experiencing serious mental health difficulties who need extra support.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: Dr Afifa Qazi, chief medical officer for the trust, said the opening was an important step forward and that until now women needing intensive care and support "have not been able to receive this specialist care from our team".
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: The unit is expected to provide around 2,500 bed days of care for women each year, and is due to welcome its first patient towards the end of November.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: Qazi said: "This new service means we can now provide specialist, compassionate care at a particularly difficult time in their lives.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: Two of the 10 beds will also be available to women referred by other NHS trusts, depending on individual needs.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: The trust already provides intensive mental health care for men at Willow Suite, a 12-bed unit at Littlebrook Hospital.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: The new unit extends this specialist service to women.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: The unit is expected to provide around 2,500 bed days of care for women each year.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: People with personal experience of mental health services helped shape the unit, and its design also takes account of sensory needs, including those of women with autism and learning disabilities.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: Jim Dickson, MP for Dartford, said women experiencing serious mental health difficulties deserved "care that treats them with dignity, compassion and an understanding of their individual needs".
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: "I'm pleased to see this new unit open in Dartford.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: It is an important investment in mental health services for women and their families across Kent and Medway," he said.
sentences.article_title: Psychiatric intensive care unit for women to open

sentences.text: The government has warned some schools start teaching GCSEs in the first year of secondary school Secondary schools will be told not to teach GCSEs early as part of a major shake-up of how children in Years 7 to 9 are taught in England.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The government plans to make Key Stage 3 a more distinct education phase, urging schools to focus less on exams and more on a "richer, more engaging" experience.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The changes come in response to two reviews that found pupils were increasingly becoming disengaged in their early teenage years, affecting attendance and achievement, the Department for Education (DfE) said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The move will mark a reversal of the approach taken by the previous Conservative government to focus the first three years of secondary school on core subjects and on doing well in assessments.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: Former Education Secretary Michael Gove prioritised English, maths and science, while raising grade boundaries, making exams harder and limiting resits.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: He also made GCSEs linear, meaning they are sat all in one go at the end of Year 11 instead of over the course of Key Stage 4.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: These reforms meant teachers started preparing pupils for exams at an earlier stage at the expense of teaching unexamined parts of their subject.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The DfE has pledged a "more engaging offer" in subjects like drama, PE, music and languages, which have seen a decline in students taking them, when it publishes its new curriculum later this year.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: It says persistent absence nearly doubles among pupils between Year 6 and Year 9.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: The department pointed to a recent survey commissioned by the International Baccalaureate that found GCSE prep dominated Key Stage 3 learning in England, with 57% of teachers saying it was the leading influence on the curriculum.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: "The pressures of GCSEs and an overcrowded curriculum are resulting in too many children receiving a narrower offer during Key Stage 3 and being rushed towards exams without grasping the fundamentals or developing deeper understanding," Powell said.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: "I'm putting a stop to that." A 2015 Ofsted report suggested that Key Stage 3 may be "wasted years", echoing the view at the time that pupils aged 11-14 lacked a clear motivation to work hard.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: However, the government faced criticism at the time that its reforms made each exam far more significant, meaning teachers refocused lessons only on what could come up in them.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: Reacting to the DfE's announcement on Sunday, Lib Dem education spokeswoman Munira Wilson MP said school was "more than drilling kids for exams" but cautioned against "micromanaging" teachers.
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: She added that a new curriculum "alone won't get children back into the classroom", noting that "too many pupils are missing school because of anxiety and unmet mental health needs" while "schools can't offer more drama, music and languages without the teachers to teach them".
sentences.article_title: Secondary schools told to stop teaching GCSEs before Year 10

sentences.text: Ellie Goudie (L), who is pictured with her mother Kerry, turned to a rage room after her brother died When Ellie Goudie's brother Ryan died aged 23, she could not bear the thought of anyone else having his belongings.
sentences.article_title: 'My brother died, so I smashed up his TV'

sentences.text: Instead, she paid to smash them to pieces.
sentences.article_title: 'My brother died, so I smashed up his TV'

sentences.text: Armed with a baseball bat in a Swindon rage room, Ellie destroyed some of the possessions Ryan had left behind, including his beloved television, saying it helped her cope with the pain of losing him.

sentences.text: He can't have it any more, so no one should," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My brother died, so I smashed up his TV'

sentences.text: He probably was doing it with me," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My brother died, so I smashed up his TV'

sentences.article_title: 'My brother died, so I smashed up his TV'

sentences.text: Operators say many visitors are seeking an emotional release during some of the most difficult periods of their lives, including bereavement, trauma, relationship breakdowns and stress.
sentences.article_title: 'My brother died, so I smashed up his TV'

sentences.article_title: 'My brother died, so I smashed up his TV'

sentences.text: "Some people are quite reserved when they come in, and then when I go and speak to them after they have a big smile on their face." he said.
sentences.article_title: 'My brother died, so I smashed up his TV'

sentences.article_title: 'My brother died, so I smashed up his TV'

sentences.article_title: 'My brother died, so I smashed up his TV'

sentences.article_title: 'My brother died, so I smashed up his TV'

sentences.text: Several universities in England have only been using below-average salaries in examples of student loan repayments on their websites, the BBC has found.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Treasury Committee chair Dame Meg Hillier, who led a recent inquiry into student loans, said some information about repayments was "misleading", including one instance where they were compared to the "cost of a daily coffee".
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: She also said the Department for Education (DfE) must include higher-salary examples on its own website, too.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The DfE said it would review the information it provides, while universities said their websites referred to government information and would be reviewed where necessary.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Student loan repayments are tied to earnings, so the more you earn, the more you repay every month - and graduates generally go on to earn more than non-graduates.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Current and prospective students in England take out Plan 5 loans to pay for their tuition fees and living costs.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: They repay 9% of anything they earn over £25,000 for 40 years, or until the loan is paid off.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The BBC looked at publicly available information on more than 110 university websites in England and found cases of inaccurate information about the salary at which they start repaying and the length of time they repay for.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: It also found that 12 universities only gave students worked examples of repayments based on earnings that are less than the UK average, which is £39,039.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Northumbria University's website said those graduates would be "repaying an amount less than the cost of a daily coffee" - a comparison that has been removed since the university was contacted by the BBC.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The DfE website also only gives examples of monthly repayments for people earning up to £38,400 on other student loan plans, but does not include any real-world repayment examples for Plan 5 students.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Repayments are 9% of earnings over £25,000, so someone earning £30,000 will repay £37.50 per month, but someone earning £100,000 will repay £562.50 per month.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Megan Russon, 21, is a recently graduated tax accountant from Cannock with a starting salary of around £29,000, meaning she will repay about £30 a month.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: However, she expects to earn around £50,000 when she becomes chartered in three years' time, and will be repaying about £187 per month.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Megan owes about £62,000 after graduating from the University of Birmingham with a degree in accounting and finance Megan says universities gave examples of repayments based on earnings of between £25,000 and £45,000 at open days and said graduates "wouldn't even notice the repayments because they should be minimal".
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: "At the time, I wasn't sure what salary I was even going to be on when I graduated," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: The University of Exeter said Plan 5 loans were written off a decade earlier than they actually are, Royal Holloway and Edge Hill listed the wrong repayment thresholds, and Harper Adams said students from England were still on Plan 2 loans.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: All four universities have updated their websites since being contacted by the BBC.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: "I'm pretty shocked at what the BBC has uncovered here and I'm going to be raising it with the relevant MPs and urging them to write to the universities in their constituencies to make them step up and do a better job," Dame Meg said.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: She said the DfE should be "taking the lead" by reflecting repayments for higher earners, but that universities also "have a responsibility to the young people that they're taking on board for the three or four years of their degree".
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Will we ever pay back our student loans?
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: England's controversial student loans system has left many graduates frustrated.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Dame Meg chaired an inquiry into student loans this year and said the DfE had been "mis-selling" Plan 2 loans , which were given between 2012 and 2023 in England and are still issued in Wales.

sentences.text: Her report said the DfE had not made clear how higher earnings would affect monthly repayments and criticised comparisons to £30-a-month phone contracts.

sentences.text: We are also working with universities to ensure the information they provide to students is clear and up to date," it added.
sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.article_title: 'Misleading' student loans information left out examples of higher-salary repayments

sentences.text: Ofcom has set out its recommendations for the most effective ways to identify which of the UK's millions of social media users are aged over 16.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Under the UK's social media ban - which is due to come into force in March next year - those under that age will be prevented from accessing ten of the biggest platforms, including Instagram, TikTok and Snapchat.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Many UK adults are also likely to have to confirm that they are not under-age by using one of the proposed measures, which are subject to government approval.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: A similar ban was introduced in Australia last year but many children there have found ways to get round it .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: The UK says it intends to take a tougher approach.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Age verification below 18 is challenging because 16 and 17 year olds don't have credit cards or full driving licences, and may not have passports either.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: They can also look significantly older or younger than they are.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: However, ultimately it will be up to the tech companies to figure out how to implement the checks: the onus is on social network providers to come up with their own solutions and comply.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Meta told the BBC it already applies some methods recommended by Ofcom to enforce its user age requirements or place users in Teen Accounts settings.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: But it said applying age checks at device-level, via app stores, could reduce the burden on people to have to repeatedly verify their age across multiple platforms.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: This would place responsibility with Apple and Google, who between them operate most of the world's smartphones.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Apple has already introduced age verification in the UK .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: However Ofcom says that would not absolve the social network providers from doing their own checks as well.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Dawes said making the ban work would be a joint effort.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "At Ofcom, what we will do is make sure that the services that the social media companies put in the checks that they need to," she told BBC News.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "That's our job, but the wider question about how everybody engages with this, it is for everybody, really.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Child safety campaigners including the Molly Rose Foundation and NSPCC welcomed Ofcom's guidance.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: But both said there were lessons to be learned from how Australia's social media ban had been implemented, after it was found many under-16s could still access social platforms .
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "That's why, as we prepare to embark on our own social media ban in the UK, we need to make sure we accurately know the age of child users," said Rani Govender, head of child safety online at the NSPCC.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: She said the government and Ofcom must ensure tech firms are held accountable for meeting age check standards "to help keep children safe online and ensure the ban delivers change in practice".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: But Andy Burrows, the Molly Rose Foundation's chief executive, said Ofcom had shown a "dire track record" of enforcing the Online Safety Act - raising questions over how effectively it would help deliver a social media ban.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "Andy Burnham must deliver a ban that learns the lessons from Australia and that incentivises safety-by-design as the price of admission to the UK market, with a ban as the starting point in a proper plan to give children a safe and happy online life," he said.
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: Jonny Bunt, corporate affairs director of BT's consumer division, said families should "prepare children for life online after the ban and highlight the risks of trying to dodge the restrictions".
sentences.article_title: Ofcom outlines age check methods ahead of social media ban for under-16s

sentences.text: "Having those conversations now and giving young people time to prepare for the changes in March will be crucial in helping them adapt to a significant change for a whole generation," he said.

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell says the government will "update and strengthen" Holocaust education within schools after a major review highlighted the "shocking scale" of antisemitism in British society.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Schools and colleges in England will be required to recognise antisemitism as a distinct category of harm and take explicit action against it.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It means anti-Jewish hatred will be treated as a specific safeguarding risk rather than being dealt with through existing measures to stop racism and bullying.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The government has accepted all of the 27 recommendations made in the government-commissioned review including dedicated training for teachers and more consistent recording of incidents.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Schools should recognise antisemitism as distinct form of harm, review says The review into antisemitism in schools and colleges in England was led by former Ofsted chief inspector Sir David Bell and presented to Parliament on Wednesday.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Powell told the BBC it marked a "generational moment" to re-educate young people, among whom she said the issue of antisemitism was "particularly prevalent".
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: She said: "It's definitely a crisis and I think it's actually got worse since Sir David began this review.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: This has become a real challenge for Jewish people in our country, but also Jewish students and Jewish teachers working in our schools and colleges.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: "I do really feel it is a generational moment to educate this generation and the next – that is the job of education – to understand what antisemitism is in the modern world." Speaking on Holocaust education, the education secretary said new lessons will "challenge" some of the concepts that young people have.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review also calls for stronger guidance on political impartiality for teachers.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Powell told the House of Commons "teachers should not bring their own political views into the classroom" but they should not avoid discussing important topics.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The review was launched following a series of high-profile incidents including the attack at Heaton Park synagogue in Manchester in October 2025, in which two men were killed.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: Separate reviews were also commissioned into antisemitism in healthcare and into public order and hate crime laws.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: The BBC revealed in August that the Bell review had found Jewish schoolchildren were experiencing regular harassment and abuse.
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review

sentences.text: It also found that headteachers of some Jewish schools were spending more of their time dealing with security arrangements than educational matters .
sentences.article_title: Holocaust school lessons to be improved after 'shocking' antisemitism review
